title: The God Who Reigns Alone
description: The God Who Reigns Alone in Tonic Solfa to QUAM DILECTA, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Drummond of Hawthornden wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 137 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Unity of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sixes (6.6.6.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to QUAM DILECTA; any other Sixes tune fits them as well.
underlay: The God who reigns a-lone O'er earth, and sea, and sky, Let man with prais-es own, And sound his hon-ors high.

lines: O'er earth, and sea, and sky,

licence: Public domain: William Drummond of Hawthornden died in 1649.
credits: Words by William Drummond of Hawthornden (1585–1649), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to QUAM DILECTA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
